title: Capability Gating and Gradual Rollout Playbook for Multi-Variant Inference
author: Marina Kovács
body:
Summary

This playbook defines a cross-cutting, operationally safe pattern for gating, rolling out, and retiring capability-level changes in the Redwood inference stack. It covers API contract changes that enable/disable model capabilities, runtime and infra gating, telemetry and SLI mapping, performance guardrails, and a prescriptive checklist for canary, ramp and rollback. The aim is to let product and ML teams ship behavioral feature changes (e.g., new tool-calls, structured-output modes, higher-fidelity model variants) with minimal user impact and clear operational controls.

Goals

- Provide a single reproducible rollout model that spans API, runtime, infra and observability.
- Ensure changes are reversible and observable with clear SLO/alert mappings.
- Minimize blast radius using capability scoping and tiered exposure.
- Make performance and cost impacts explicit before wide exposure.

Scope and Non-goals

Scope:
- Capability-level changes that affect inference behavior, routing, or output schema (not purely UI changes).
- Multi-variant serving (A/B, canary, staged rollout) where variants may differ by model version, quantization, or runtime feature.

Non-goals:
- Authorization or RBAC mechanics (see rbac-and-auth).
- Long-term feature flag system design (assume we use the platform feature-flag service).

Key Definitions

- Capability: A named, discoverable runtime behavior toggle exposed to clients (example: "structured-tool-calls-v2").
- Gate: Logical control that enables or disables a capability at API, tenant, or request scope.
- Variant: A specific implementation of a capability (model v3 vs model v2 quantized).

Principles and Decision Rationale

1) Capability identifiers are stable, namespaced, and part of the API manifest. They are the atomic unit for rollout and telemetry.
2) Runtime and infra must honor API-scoped gates to guarantee predictable routing and costing.
3) Observability must map capability usage to the SLO and cost telemetry so decisions are evidence driven.
4) Rollouts must be staged with automated rollback triggers driven by SLI degradation and regression tests.

Policy: API Contract and Header Conventions

- Capability header: Accept-Redwood-Capabilities: structured-tool-calls-v2;enable=true;variant=canary
- If the client omits the header, the server uses tenant-level defaults.
- Capability discovery endpoint: GET /v1/capabilities returns manifest (name, stable_since, variants, compatibility_notes).
- When a capability changes output schema, the response must include schema-version in the response envelope ("schema_version": "2.1"). Backwards-compatible changes must be annotated in the manifest.

Implementation Patterns (API | Runtime | Infra | Observability | Performance)

A. API layer
- Validate capability header early; fail fast with 400 + error_code="capability_unknown" if unknown.
- Support layered defaults: request header -> tenant default -> global default.
- Return an "X-Redwood-Active-Capabilities" response header summarizing the effective flags and resolved variants for debugging.

B. Runtime routing and model-serving
- Runtime must accept an opaque capability token provided by the API gateway to make routing decisions without re-parsing user headers.
- Variant matching order: exact variant -> tenant pinned variant -> fallback variant.
- Batching: ensure batching logic groups only compatible variants. If variant mixing occurs, either split batches (preferred) or honor the lowest-fidelity variant and mark telemetry.

C. Infrastructure and capacity
- Capacity planning must provision canary capacity (5% baseline) and burst buffers for ramp.
- Pre-warm model artifacts for intended variants during canary to avoid cold-starts.
- Quotas and cost controls: canaries should be limited by token budget and compute budget to avoid runaway billing.

D. Observability and SLI mapping
- Telemetry must include these dimensions on every request: capability_name, variant, tenant_id, latency_ms_p95, tokens_consumed.
- Mapped SLIs (minimum):
  - request_success_rate (>= 99.5% during ramp)
  - p95_latency_ms (must not exceed baseline + 40%)
  - output_schema_validation_fail_rate (< 0.1%)
  - quality_regression_score (derived from prompt-set evals, fail if delta > 3 points)

E. Performance and cost guardrails
- Define a before/after performance baseline with automated perf-test harness (synthetic workload approximating production distribution).
- If cost per 1k tokens increases by > 15% for canary traffic, require explicit approval to proceed.

Example Capability Manifest (YAML snippet)

---
name: structured-tool-calls-v2
stable_since: 2026-02
variants:
  - name: stable
    description: default server-side implementation, conservative latency
    cost_multiplier: 1.0
  - name: canary
    description: experimental model with structured output; higher fidelity
    cost_multiplier: 1.28
compatibility_notes: "Produces schema_version 2.x for tool outputs; backwards compatibility shim available."

Telemetry SLI Table (CSV-style for quick copy)

metric,aggregation,threshold,action
request_success_rate,percent,>=99.5%,rollback
p95_latency_ms,p95,+40% vs baseline,alert-and-hold-ramp
output_schema_validation_fail_rate,percent,<0.1%,rollback
quality_regression_score,delta,<3 points,stop-ramp-and-run-eval-suite
compute_cost_per_1k_tokens,ratio,<1.15,manual-approval

Staged Rollout Recipe

1) Canary lab: run the variant with synthetic traffic in a sandbox for 48h. Gather perf, schema, quality metrics.
2) Internal QA: route 0.5% of internal tenant traffic + 1% of test tenants for 72h.
3) Customer opt-in: expose capability to a small set of paying customers (by tenant allowlist) for 7 days.
4) Gradual ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with each step at least 24h and automation verifying SLIs.
5) Final validation: run consolidated evaluation suite against production traffic prompts; record quality and cost deltas.

Automated Rollback Triggers (examples)

- request_success_rate drops below 99.5% for 30 minutes.
- p95_latency_ms exceeds baseline + 40% for two consecutive windows.
- output_schema_validation_fail_rate > 0.1% for 60 minutes.
- automated quality regression tests report delta >= 3 points after second ramp step.

Operational Runbook (Quick Steps)

1) Abort: If any automated trigger fires, execute immediate downgrade to last-known-good variant for affected tenants and mark the rollout hold.
2) Triage: Owner (service on-call) creates incident withTelemetry artifact: capability, variant, last 6h perf chart, sample payloads, schema validation errors.
3) Hotfix options: revert feature-flag state, pin tenant to previous variant, or apply runtime shim if schema mismatch.
4) Postmortem: within 72h record root cause, action items, and gating improvements.

Checklist Before Ramp

- [ ] Manifest published and referenced in API docs.
- [ ] Canary capacity reserved and artifacts pre-warmed.
- [ ] Perf harness run and baseline recorded.
- [ ] Telemetry dimensions and dashboards created.
- [ ] Regression prompt-set and automated evals added to CI.
- [ ] Cost approval obtained if cost delta > 10%.

Ownership and Escalation

- Capability owner: team that owns the product/ML change (must post owner in manifest).
- Service owner (runtime): infra/runtime on-call.
- Observability owner: eng-platform.
- Escalation: service on-call -> runtime lead -> SRE manager -> CTO on business-impacting incidents.

Testing and CI Requirements

- Unit tests for header parsing and default resolution.
- Integration tests that simulate mixed-variant batching.
- Perf tests running against representative sequence-length distributions.
- End-to-end evals with labeled prompt-sets; coverage for critical customer flows.

Retirement and Cleanup

- After 3 months of stable 100% traffic and zero compatibility issues, the capability owner must archive the canary variant and mark the manifest "stable".
- Feature flags should not be left permanently in allowlists; schedule a cleanup ticket at 90 days.

Appendix: Example HTTP exchange

Request:
POST /v1/generate
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer <token>
  Accept-Redwood-Capabilities: structured-tool-calls-v2;enable=true;variant=canary
Body: {"prompt": "Call tool X with args"}

Response headers:
  X-Redwood-Active-Capabilities: structured-tool-calls-v2=canary;schema_version=2.1

Response body (partial):
{"schema_version":"2.1","result":{"tool_call":{"name":"X","args":{"foo":"bar"},"confidence":0.92}}}

Appendix: Common failure modes and mitigations

- Mixed-variant batching causes high-latency tail: mitigate by enforcing strict batch-splitting at the runtime admission layer.
- Schema drift after model change: enable compatibility shim that maps old schema to new shape for 7-day grace period and require owner to ship migration changelog.
- Cost spike: auto-throttle canary traffic and escalate to cost owner; require manual approval to continue.
